The desk combines AI signals with manual control. Newcomers can start on the practice account, fund US$250 when ready, and trade 10 assets through the partner broker.
The scorecard reflects what the platform publishes, not what its ads promise. We checked the claims against the pages, looked for independent verification, and marked the gaps we found.
whatItClaims: 10 crypto assets through broker partners.
A free demo account with practice funds.
Around-the-clock support through the partner desk.
Signals generated without manual chart reading.
A US$250 minimum deposit to start.
whatWeChecked: The support channels: live chat, email or phone availability.
The fine print: clauses that qualify the headline promises.
The fee framing: no platform fees, but spreads embedded in every trade.
The support story: around-the-clock coverage claimed, exact figures conflicting.
The geo-restrictions: two lists on the page that do not agree.
The template marks: unfilled placeholders left in the wording.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Open the signup page, enter your information and confirm the account by email.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Deposit the US$250 minimum by bank card, bank transfer, PayPal or Skrill.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Configure the risk settings and mode, and keep the demo open while the live account warms up.

pros: Free registration and a demo account.
cons: Marketing numbers that the fine print walks back.
No independent audit of the models.
Registration details not stated up front.
redFlags: The fee that is not a fee: spreads embedded in every trade.
Restriction lists that name different countries.
Payout promises with no processing detail.

faqs.q: Where is The New Bitcoin Loophole restricted?
faqs.a: The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.

faqs.q: Is registration free?
faqs.a: Yes - signup is free and activates through a confirmation link. The first cost is the US$250 deposit, which stays in your trading balance.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$250, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.

bottomLine: The platform itself is workable - the dashboard, the demo and the two trading modes are all present. The caution applies to the claims around them, not the mechanics.
The scorecard settles at 4.6. That is a cautious pass - proceed with the demo first, the minimum deposit second, and treat every payout figure as unproven until you see it yourself.
